request.prompt:
You are clustering code review findings from the same PR. For each PAIR below, decide whether the two findings describe the SAME underlying issue — same root cause in the same code location. Different wording is fine. A finding about a DIFFERENT defect in the same file or function is NOT the same issue. Severity or aspect differences of the same root cause ARE the same issue.


For THIS scoring pass, duplicate equivalence is stricter than sharing a root cause.
You must compare the COMPLETE MATERIAL CLAIMS, including mechanism, triggering
conditions, execution path, and consequence. The same line or broad concern does
not establish equivalence. A report of wrong-category selection, a case/rename
mismatch, a crash, and a silent fallback are different claims even at one lookup.
An inactive/unbound API concern and an alleged active user-facing failure differ.
A compound report with an additional material claim does NOT equal its subset.
Differences only in wording, severity, or hedging do not create separate claims.
If the claimed mechanisms, triggers or consequences conflict, or one report adds
an unsupported/different material factual claim, return same=false. You are NOT
verifying which claim is true; do not repair or reinterpret either report to make
them match. If unsure whether their full claims are equivalent, return false.

For every numbered pair, extract what A and B actually CLAIM into mechanism,
trigger and consequence. Then list material_differences and give your equivalence
verdict, confidence and reason. same=true requires no material differences.
Return ONLY this JSON object, with EVERY pair index exactly once:

PAIR 15:
A: poll_feed has no error handling around open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) or SimpleRSS.parse, and the job sets retry: false. A transient feed outage (timeout, DNS failure, malformed XML) raises, the run is not retried, and the failure is invisible except in logs — an operator with feed_polling_enabled gets no signal that imports stopped, and topics silently diverge from the feed for up to an hour (or indefinitely if the feed stays broken).
B: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has no exception handling for fetch/parse failures, and the job sets `retry: false`. A transient network failure or malformed feed response on the hourly poll raises out of execute and is swallowed (retry disabled), so feed import stalls until the next hour with no logging, error notification, or backoff; the operator cannot distinguish 'feed unchanged' from 'poller broken'.

PAIR 16:
A: ensure_embeddable compares URI(request.referer).host by exact string equality with SiteSetting.embeddable_host, with no normalization for case, port, or www prefix, and the setting has no place to express scheme or port. An embedding site served from www.eviltrout.com, from a non-default port, or with an uppercase host configured fails the referer check and 404s its embeds; conversely the same loose equality is the only access control for the endpoint, so the drift between how operators type the setting and how browsers emit referers decides who can embed — a configuration minefield rather than a real invariant.
B: invalid_host? repeats the same unnormalized comparison (SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host), so any case/scheme/www divergence between the setting and the embed_url the blog's template emits makes the retriever refuse the URL. The URL is never imported and the embed page reloads the loading view every 30 seconds indefinitely, re-enqueueing RetrieveTopic jobs that always no-op — a permanent 'Loading Discussion...' widget driven by a one-character configuration mismatch.

The intended conditional-fetch check was silently dropped, so every hourly run (and every retrieve-triggered run inside TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve) re-parses the entire feed and re-processes every item, and the next reader must reverse-engineer whether feed_key was supposed to gate something.

The operator who enables feed polling with a wrong username gets a completely no-op importer with zero feedback: the scheduled job 'succeeds' hourly, nothing is ever imported, and no log, error, or failure entry distinguishes this state from a working but idle feed.
